newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Deutsche - earnings not hurt by MGAM funds crisis.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche - earnings not hurt by MGAM funds crisis.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG management board member Rolf Breuer said on Tuesday that the bank's earnings would not be damaged by the recent problems at its London funds unit, Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM).
Breuer, who heads Deutsche's global fund management business, was speaking at a presentation to analysts in Zurich, which was also attended by journalists.
Deutsche had injected 180 million stg into three MGAM funds after they were temporarily suspended pending a probe into alleged irregularities in the funds' management.
"There is no impact on our earnings," Breuer said of the incident which led to the suspension of two fund managers and prompted Deutsche to pledge it will tighten controls of MGAM from Frankfurt.
"The incident is not so much a financial problem for Deutsche Bank. The damage to our reputation is more weighty, and this cannot be calculated," Breuer said.
Damage to institutional client business had been limited but MGAM's retail business had "come into question", he added.
Deutsche had not yet established how much the securities it had taken over from the MGAM funds were worth and how much could be realised from their sale.
The 180 million stg ($280 million) injection was used to buy up the large volume of unlisted securities contained in the disputed MGAM funds.
